sections.h2: Commerce City housing at a glance
sections.html:
North of Denver, Commerce City is a home rule city inside Adams County and one of the faster-growing places on the Front Range. The 2020 census found 62,418 people, 35.9% more than in 2010, and the 2025 estimate of 72,345 adds another 15.9%.

Owners dominate: 77.2% of homes are lived in by their owners (2020 to 2024), and the median value is $499,700. Most people selling here are homeowners with equity to protect, not landlords. Think of the median as a rough reference. Your own house will land above or below it.

Refining and logistics define the local economy. Suncor Energy's refinery handles 98,000 barrels a day and is described as the biggest in the Rocky Mountain region. In 2022, transportation and warehousing receipts were about $1.46 billion, dwarfing the $91 million in health care and social assistance.

Buyers who dislike living near a refinery or an industrial corridor may pass on a house in those areas. Owners in that position sometimes find a buyer who purchases as is and has no opinion about the setting.

Once a deadline passes, delinquent interest starts. State law (section 39-10-104.5) uses the same February, April and June dates and charges interest of 1% per month on late amounts. Anyone wanting to dodge the fees tied to the tax lien sale should pay by 5:00 PM on October 31. Current details are on the Adams County due dates page.

sections.h2: Prorations and liens when the house sells
sections.html: The title company divides this year's tax between you and the buyer on closing day. Older years need to be settled already, because any lien recorded against the parcel must be released first. If you cannot tell whether a balance is open, have the title officer check before a date is set.

Nightly rentals have been allowed in Commerce City since January 1, 2025, within zoning and licensing limits. The city counts a stay of fewer than 30 days in a duplex or detached house as short term.

  • The license costs $150, lasts a year from issue and must be renewed annually.
  • A responsible agent has to be reachable 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and must live within 30 miles.
  • The city's eTRAKiT system takes applications and handles them in the order received.
  • Rules on HOAs, parking and guest limits are in Ordinances 2648 and 2653.

Maybe the house came to you with a nightly rental past. If so, make sure the license history is clean before you sell.

sections.h2: Which school district is my house in?
sections.html: Adams County School District 27J covers some of the city and Adams 14 covers the rest. Adams City High School belongs to Adams 14, and its building at 72nd and Quebec opened in 2009. Families house-hunting tend to ask, so find your street on the district map ahead of time.

July afternoons top out near 88 degrees, and winter nights fall to 21 or 22. A house that endures both gets a close look at its furnace, air conditioner and exposed plumbing. Repair a failing unit only if you are going to list. Someone paying cash simply takes the house as it is.

Late balances are common and manageable. Interest builds at 1% per month, so waiting costs money. The October 31 cutoff is the last practical day to avoid lien sale fees. Selling does not wipe out the debt. The county is paid from your proceeds at closing, so you receive less but hand over a clean title.

Phone the Adams County Treasurer for an exact payoff and pass the figure to the title company on day one. With that single number, everyone can plan the closing date and your proceeds.

Inherited houses and investor purchases sometimes carry a history of Airbnb-style stays. A buyer, and any lender behind them, will want to know whether the property held the right license, whether the responsible agent rule was followed and whether an HOA or neighbors ever complained. Pull together license renewals and any city notices before listing. A buyer who accepts the house as it stands cares less about a thin paper trail than one who needs a loan.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Commerce City house?
sections.html:
The choices are a listing, a sale on your own or an as-is cash purchase. Since most local owners hold real equity, weigh the money left after costs rather than the headline figure.

Listing means open houses and inspection requests. Selling for cash avoids both, and the closing date follows your calendar. We buy houses in Commerce City in any condition, and our offer carries no obligation.

Every seller meets the state documentary fee on a deed, which is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500. County recording pages describe it that way, and it shows up on the settlement statement beside the prorated taxes.

Net proceeds are the honest yardstick. A listing may show a larger price, but subtract agent costs, repairs requested after the inspection, the monthly cost of carrying the house, and the chance that a buyer's loan falls through. A cash offer starts lower with fewer deductions and a date you control. Get each in writing, run the same subtractions on both, and see which leaves you better placed.

Before the title officer calls, find four things: your latest Adams County tax statement, loan payoff details if you still owe on the house, any license or permit paperwork tied to rentals or repairs, and a list of everyone whose name is on the deed. Missing items are not fatal. Say what is missing at the start, and the title company can usually track down copies while the sale moves ahead.

sections.h2: Steps in a Commerce City cash sale
sections.html:
1. Give us the address and describe the house, mentioning anything unusual such as past nightly rentals or an industrial neighbor.
  2. We review the details and write an offer.
  3. Once you accept, a title company searches for liens and checks the tax position with Adams County.
  4. You sign on the date you chose, and the deed is recorded.
  5. Proceeds reach you after any tax or lien balance is paid.

You can say no, and asking costs nothing. A written offer lets you set it against a listing on equal terms.

faqs.q: How many people live in Commerce City?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 62,418 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 72,345.

faqs.q: What are the Adams County property tax deadlines?
faqs.a: February 28 and June 15 for two payments, or April 30 for one full payment. The county does not accept partial payments.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Commerce City?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024 is $499,700. Your house may differ, so use it only as a benchmark.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Commerce City house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a $150 license, renewed each year, and a responsible agent who lives within 30 miles and can respond around the clock.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Commerce City house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Adams County School District 27J and Adams 14 each cover part of the city, so use the district's boundary lookup.
